label: Owner-alpha adult competency-floor research batch 1

source_catalog.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription
source_catalog.table_locator: Table 3.8, Treadmill-Based Cardiorespiratory Fitness Classifications by Age and Sex
source_catalog.source_population: FRIEND Registry adults considered free from known cardiovascular disease; ages 30-39 included 1,473 males and 1,043 females.
source_catalog.reported_value: At the 55th percentile, directly measured treadmill VO2max was 41.6 mL/kg/min for males and 29.7 mL/kg/min for females aged 30-39.
limitations: The values require directly measured maximal treadmill testing.
Cardiorespiratory reference status is not a complete general-athleticism standard.

source_catalog.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription
source_catalog.table_locator: Table 3.10, Fitness Categories for Grip Strength by Sex and Age
source_catalog.source_population: Adults in age- and sex-stratified grip-strength reference data; the textbook table does not reproduce recruitment details or subgroup sample sizes.
source_catalog.reported_value: The 50th-percentile best-hand values for ages 35-39 are 48 kg for males and 28 kg for females.
limitations: Best score from either hand can hide side-to-side differences.
Dynamometer setup and device affect comparability.

source_catalog.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription
source_catalog.table_locator: Table 3.11 and Box 3.10, Push-up Test by Age and Sex
source_catalog.source_population: Canadian Society for Exercise Physiology age- and sex-category reference data; subgroup sampling details are not reproduced in the table.
source_catalog.reported_value: For ages 30-39, the Good category begins at 17 standard push-ups for males and 13 modified knee push-ups for females.
limitations: The male and female rows use different movement protocols and are not directly comparable.
The source notes that broader female standard-push-up norms are still needed.

source_catalog.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription
source_catalog.table_locator: Table 3.12 and Box 3.11, Countermovement Vertical Jump by Age and Sex
source_catalog.source_population: Age- and sex-stratified countermovement-jump reference categories; sample sizes and recruitment are not reproduced in the table.
source_catalog.reported_value: For ages 30-39, the Good category begins at 40 cm for males and 28 cm for females.
limitations: The measure uses arm swing and best of three trials.
Wall/chalk and commercial apparatus measurements may not be interchangeable.

source_catalog.title: Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning
source_catalog.table_locator: Table 14.34, Normative Data for the Balance Error Scoring System Test
source_catalog.source_population: Adults in age- and sex-stratified BESS reference data summarized from Iverson and Koehle (2013); sample details are not reproduced in the table.
source_catalog.reported_value: For ages 30-39, errors were 11.4 ± 5.6 for women and 11.5 ± 5.5 for men.
limitations: Seventeen errors is a rounded mean-plus-one-SD derivation, not a published cutoff.
BESS performance is protocol- and surface-specific.

source_catalog.title: Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning
source_catalog.table_locator: Table 14.14, Descriptive Data for the 300-Yard Shuttle Test
source_catalog.source_population: Eighty-one recreational male and female athletes in the cited descriptive dataset.
source_catalog.reported_value: Recreational athletes completed the 300-yard shuttle in 72.8 ± 9.1 seconds.
limitations: The book explicitly labels these values descriptive, not normative.
The source does not provide an age-specific owner match in the table.

source_catalog.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription
source_catalog.table_locator: Figure 3.3, Bench Press Weight Ratio by Age and Sex
source_catalog.source_population: Adults in age- and sex-stratified Universal DVR machine bench-press data.
source_catalog.reported_value: The figure presents percentile curves for machine 1RM bench-press load divided by body weight.
limitations: The proposed 1.0 ratio is not extracted from the figure.
Universal DVR machine values must not be represented as free-weight norms.

source_catalog.title: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription
source_catalog.table_locator: Figure 3.4, Leg Press Weight Ratio by Age and Sex
source_catalog.source_population: Predominantly white, college-educated adults in Universal DVR machine leg-press data.
source_catalog.reported_value: The figure presents percentile curves for machine 1RM leg-press load divided by body weight.
limitations: The proposed 1.5 free-weight squat ratio is not extracted from the figure.
Machine leg press and free-weight squat are not interchangeable tests.

source_catalog.title: Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning
source_catalog.table_locator: Table 14.30, Percentile Ranks for the 5-10-5 Test
source_catalog.source_population: NCAA Division I volleyball, basketball, softball, baseball, and American football athletes.
source_catalog.reported_value: The slowest 10th-percentile sport/sex cell reported is 5.55 seconds for women's softball.
limitations: Elite collegiate athletes are a poor match for a recreationally trained working adult.
Sport, sex, surface, footwear, and electronic timing materially affect the comparison.

proposals.label: Treadmill VO2max · male reference · age 30-39
proposals.threshold_rationale: Uses the table's 55th percentile, labeled Fair, as a reviewable no-major-weak-link proposal rather than an athletic ideal.
proposals.population_match_notes: Age matches and the cohort was free from known cardiovascular disease, but it was not selected for physical work or recreational training.
proposals.evidence_gap: No source validates the 55th percentile as AGAS's minimum useful competency.
prerequisites_before_release: Record an applicable sex-classification observation without inferring it from name or appearance.
Govern a maximal treadmill protocol and clinical-risk screening; do not self-administer maximal testing by default.
does_not_establish: Medical safety, exercise clearance, or a workout dose.
Equivalence with an estimated field-test VO2max.
review_questions: Is Fair/55th percentile too low for this owner's competency floor?
Should AGAS prefer a governed submaximal field estimate instead of direct maximal testing?

proposals.label: Consecutive standard push-ups · male reference · age 30-39
proposals.measurement: Consecutive standard push-ups without rest under Box 3.10 technique
proposals.threshold_rationale: Uses the lower bound of the source's Good category rather than the boundary between Poor and Fair.
proposals.population_match_notes: Age matches; occupational and recreational-training characteristics are unknown.
proposals.evidence_gap: The category is a reference classification, not a validated AGAS minimum or dose rule.
prerequisites_before_release: Record an applicable sex-classification observation.

proposals.label: Consecutive modified push-ups · female reference · age 30-39
proposals.measurement: Consecutive modified knee push-ups without rest under Box 3.10 technique
proposals.threshold_rationale: Uses the lower bound of the source's Good category while preserving the source's distinct modified protocol.
proposals.population_match_notes: Age matches, but a modified protocol may have poor construct relevance for a recreationally trained physical worker.
proposals.evidence_gap: The source says broader female standard-push-up norms are needed; this modified test may be the wrong owner-alpha measure.
prerequisites_before_release: Record an applicable sex-classification observation.
Decide whether to reject the sex-differentiated protocol and research standard-push-up norms instead.
does_not_establish: Equivalence to standard push-ups.
A push-up exercise prescription.
review_questions: Should this candidate be rejected in favor of one standard protocol for everyone?
If retained, is the modified protocol relevant to the owner's actual abilities?

proposals.label: BESS errors · sex-neutral derived reference · age 30-39
proposals.measurement: Balance Error Scoring System total errors under the source protocol
proposals.threshold_rationale: Rounds mean plus one standard deviation to 17; both sex rows converge on the same result, but the source does not define it as a cutoff.
proposals.population_match_notes: Age matches; the source table does not establish similarity in training history, occupation, or prior balance exposure.
proposals.evidence_gap: The derivation is an engineering choice and needs protocol/applicability review.
prerequisites_before_release: Govern exact BESS positions, surfaces, error rules, and self-scoring reliability.
Establish symptom and fall-risk exclusions.
does_not_establish: Neurologic diagnosis, concussion status, or fall clearance.
General coordination across moving tasks.
review_questions: Is mean plus one SD too permissive for a no-major-weak-link floor?
Is self-scored BESS reliable enough for this product?

proposals.label: 300-yard shuttle · recreational-athlete derived reference
proposals.measurement: 300-yard shuttle completion time under the cited protocol
proposals.threshold_rationale: Uses the recreational-athlete mean plus one SD (72.8 + 9.1 seconds) as a deliberately provisional lower-performance boundary.
proposals.population_match_notes: Recreational-athlete status is relevant, but age, occupation, surface, and conditioning history are unspecified.
proposals.evidence_gap: The book explicitly says the data are descriptive rather than normative; the derived boundary is not validated.
prerequisites_before_release: Govern high-intensity eligibility, surface, course length, turns, timing, and termination criteria.
Earn acceleration/deceleration exposure before selecting this test.
does_not_establish: Aerobic capacity or sprint speed in isolation.
Readiness for repeated maximal shuttles.
review_questions: Is this unnecessarily fatiguing for initial assessment?
Should a lower-risk repeated-effort protocol be researched instead?

proposals.label: Free-weight back squat 1RM · professional-judgment proposal
proposals.measurement: Free-weight back squat 1RM divided by contemporaneous body mass
proposals.threshold_rationale: A concrete review target for a broadly useful high-force reserve; it is not attributed to either textbook and is intentionally awaiting accountable adoption or revision.
proposals.population_match_notes: No reviewed population source in this batch supports a sex-neutral 1.5 ratio for this owner.
proposals.evidence_gap: The ACSM figure is machine leg press data and does not support this free-weight squat number.
prerequisites_before_release: An accountable reviewer must author and attest the professional-judgment authority.
Govern technique, depth, familiarization, spotting, and eligibility; consider a submaximal estimate.
does_not_establish: A scientific norm, safety cutoff, or universal athletic standard.
Equivalence to machine leg press.
review_questions: Keep, change, or reject 1.5 times body mass?
Should this use a technically valid 3-5RM estimate rather than direct 1RM?

proposals.label: Free-weight bench press 1RM · professional-judgment proposal
proposals.measurement: Free-weight bench press 1RM divided by contemporaneous body mass
proposals.threshold_rationale: A concrete review target for upper-body force relative to mass; it is not attributed to the machine-based ACSM curves.
proposals.population_match_notes: No reviewed population source in this batch supports a sex-neutral 1.0 ratio for this owner.
proposals.evidence_gap: The ACSM figure is Universal DVR machine data and does not support this free-weight number.
prerequisites_before_release: An accountable reviewer must author and attest the professional-judgment authority.
Govern technique, familiarization, spotting, and eligibility; consider a submaximal estimate.
does_not_establish: A scientific norm, safety cutoff, or universal athletic standard.
Equivalence to machine bench press.
review_questions: Keep, change, or reject 1.0 times body mass?
Should this use a technically valid 3-5RM estimate rather than direct 1RM?

proposals.label: Loaded carry at 0.5× body mass for 100 m · professional-judgment proposal
proposals.measurement: Continuous carry distance with total external load equal to 50% of body mass
proposals.threshold_rationale: A measurable owner-review target combining meaningful relative load and locomotion; neither number is presented as a published norm.
proposals.population_match_notes: It is task-relevant to physical work, but no reviewed population reference supports the exact load-distance pair.
proposals.evidence_gap: A suitable adult loaded-carry norm was not found in the supplied textbook tables.
prerequisites_before_release: An accountable reviewer must author and attest the professional-judgment authority.
Define implement, grip allowance, turns, posture, set-down rules, and symptom stops.
does_not_establish: Occupational fitness certification or manual-handling safety.
A carry training dose.
review_questions: Is 50% body mass for 100 m useful and practical?
Should grip failure, gait quality, or completion time be separate observations?

proposals.label: Six movement-exposure families in 90 days · professional-judgment proposal
proposals.measurement: Distinct governed movement-exposure families completed in a rolling 90-day window
proposals.threshold_rationale: A concrete breadth proposal that does not confuse gym performance with exposure to varied movement problems.
proposals.population_match_notes: The construct matches the blueprint mission, but the count and time window have no reviewed population basis.
proposals.evidence_gap: No validated norm defines a useful number of movement families over 90 days.
prerequisites_before_release: An accountable reviewer must define the exposure-family ontology and attest the threshold.
Specify the minimum meaningful exposure required for a family to count.
does_not_establish: Competence, proficiency, or safety in any exposure family.
That all movement families are equally valuable.
review_questions: Are six families and 90 days the right breadth and window?
Which exposure families should count for the owner-alpha?

proposals.label: 5-10-5 change-of-direction time · low-applicability reference
proposals.threshold_rationale: Uses the slowest reported 10th-percentile cell only as a conspicuously low collegiate reference; it is included to expose, not hide, the population mismatch.
proposals.population_match_notes: NCAA Division I athletes are younger and more sport-selected than the owner; combining sex and sport cells is not validated.
proposals.evidence_gap: A directly applicable recreational adult reference and a justified sex-neutral floor are still missing.
prerequisites_before_release: Do not release without more applicable reference data or an explicit professional-judgment authority.
Govern earned sprint/deceleration exposure, surface, footwear, timing, and symptom criteria.
does_not_establish: Safe readiness for maximal cutting.
A universal agility threshold or training dose.
review_questions: Should this candidate be rejected rather than converted into a floor?
Would a lower-intensity deceleration/control assessment be better for initial planning?

release_boundary: These 15 records are research proposals only. They cannot be batch-ratified, create competency floors, satisfy planning prerequisites, select an assessment, or prescribe training. Each requires owner review; each released floor must then receive exact protocol, evidence or judgment authority, digest, attestation, and immutable persistence separately.
